claim: Retrieving one past solved task and having the LLM edit it beats zero-shot and random-case prompting on data-science code (one-pass 85% GPT-3.5, 99% GPT-4 vs best baseline 56%/60%).
agent_test: Equal-token test: edit-one-retrieved-case vs zero-shot vs best-of-N fresh samples on our task set.

claim: Removing the feedback-driven revise/edit step of a CBR pipeline hurts: DS-Agent rank 2.08 vs 2.58 (verified in paper); CBR-to-SQL execution accuracy 0.894 vs 0.786 without Revision.
agent_test: Ablate the post-retrieval edit/repair pass at equal tokens.

claim: More retrieved cases do not help adaptation: Memento peaks at K=4 (F1 64.5 vs 59.9 at K=0, 63.6 at K=1), most gain at K=1; DS-Agent falls as cases increase; fallacy-CBR best at k=1.
agent_test: Sweep K=1,2,4,8 at equal total tokens; expect plateau by K<=4.

claim: Learned adaptation helps most when the query is far from stored cases; with familiar queries a plain regressor can beat retrieve-then-adapt (face-age: regressor 5.97 vs best CBR 7.49-8.14; novel >70: Siamese 33.05->28.83).
agent_test: Split test items by distance to memory; compare edit vs direct solve per bucket.

claim: Retrieval and adaptation trained or tuned separately can be out of step, making adaptation worsen the answer (Siamese normal setting 7.49->7.86).
agent_test: Select cases by editability (adaptation-guided retrieval) vs raw similarity; compare.

claim: Error-keyed retrieval of edit operators transfers across domains where problem-text retrieval collapses (MBPP-Hard Plus: 74.36 vs 58.12 cross-domain; in-domain problem-based slightly better 97.56 vs 96.34).
agent_test: Index memory by failure signature as well as problem text; test on cross-domain items.

claim: Storing the edit (error-to-operator) rather than the whole old solution cuts tokens (-50.6% vs Momentum; 21.6k vs 43.7k) at equal or higher pass rate.
agent_test: Compare operator-memory vs full-solution memory at equal tokens.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without external feedback does not improve and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CSQA 75.8->41.8; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5->89.0); with oracle it rises.
agent_test: Any edit pass must use an external check (test, tool, verifier); test blind-edit vs verified-edit.

claim: Self-repair quality is bottlenecked by diagnosis/feedback quality: human feedback raises GPT-4 repair success 1.58x; GPT-4 feedback inaccurate 32/80 vs 7/80 and never expresses uncertainty; repair often does not beat fresh samples at equal compute.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare repair of draft vs resampling; add separate diagnosis step.

claim: Case memory adds additive gains on top of planning (Memento: HLE +4.5/+7.0, SimpleQA +3.7/+5.3, DeepResearcher +6.7/+8.2 F1/PM; GAIA 87.88 val).
agent_test: Add case memory to our planner; measure with and without at equal tokens.

claim: Workflow-style abstracted cases improve web-agent success but strict end-task gains on hard splits are small (WebArena 23.5->35.5; Mind2Web cross-task SR 2.0 vs 4.8/4.0 though step SR 36.2->45.1).
agent_test: Test abstracted workflows vs raw trajectories; report step and task success.

claim: Retrieval + LLM-as-adapter helps small models in narrow domains: DomAgent truck CAN 39.62->96.64 (Qwen7B); legal CBR-RAG +1.94% cosine; fallacy adapter +2.5 to 8 F1.
agent_test: Check that gains persist for a strong base model (GPT-4o 71->98 suggests yes, but DS-1000 only +7.6).

claim: Self-generated exemplars (recall-then-solve) can match or beat retrieved ones for strong models only; weak models gain nothing (GSM8K davinci-003 61 vs 57 retrieved; davinci-001 9 vs 11).
agent_test: Compare self-recalled vs retrieved examples on our model.

claim: LLM analogy and case-based generalisation is brittle: GPT models drop on counterfactual letter-strings (GPT-4 0.452 vs humans 0.753); fine-tuned transformers do case-based interpolation and fail in held-out regions.
agent_test: Probe edits on surface-altered variants of retrieved cases.

claim: Explicit adaptation stage makes the system more robust to loss of top retrieved cases (AccEX drop MIMICSQL 0.028 vs 0.074; EHRSQL 0.043 vs 0.138).
agent_test: Remove top-1 retrieved case; compare drop with vs without edit stage.

claim: Adaptation knowledge can be mined from case-pair differences (CDH; CABAMAKA 647 cases, 2344 closed itemsets, 208 kept; opportunistic mining at failure time), but needs expert filtering and has no accuracy figures.
agent_test: Mine edit rules from our own solved pairs; check human-verified usefulness.

claim: Failure-indexed memory (CHEF) predicts and avoids known failures before planning; only demonstrated by worked examples, no benchmark.
agent_test: Index failures by interacting goals; test pre-emptive warning vs none.

claim: Adaptation-guided retrieval (pick the most adaptable case, not the most similar) is reported to beat similarity retrieval, but no numbers were read in this subfield.
agent_test: Run similarity vs editability ranking.

claim: No head-to-head LLM study isolates the adapt step against retrieval alone; only ablations exist (CBR-to-SQL, DS-Agent, TextBFGS).
agent_test: Build that head-to-head ourselves.

claim: Editing an earlier attempt beats drawing fresh samples at equal budget when a verifier or tests exist: Self-Debugging matches 16 samples from 1 edited sample (Spider), 8 edited beat 32 fresh; Snell revision model matches best-of-N with up to 4x less compute on MATH. Not shown for a retrieved case or without a verifier.
agent_test: Equal-token test: edit-one-retrieved-case vs best-of-N fresh with the same verifier on a reasoning set.

claim: Blind LLM editing breaks correct answers at measurable rates: 38% of correct answers flipped by a naive revision model (MATH); Gemini 1.5 Flash base self-correction 15.8% correct-to-incorrect, Self-Refine 4.2%; Llama-3.1-8B 58.8% of correct answers overturned under a doubt prompt. No rate yet for retrieved-case editing.
agent_test: Measure the correct-to-incorrect rate of our edit step; always keep original unless the check passes.

claim: Raw retrieved examples can lower a strong model below its no-memory baseline (GPT-4o Game of 24 10 to 6, MMLU-Pro Eng 53.2 to 48.8, AIME full-history 20.0 to 6.7); AWM falls to 3.4 vs 10.3 no-memory on WebArena cross-site.
agent_test: Compare raw-case prompt vs no-memory vs distilled item on a strong base model; look for negative transfer.

claim: Best memory unit is task dependent. Curated or distilled items beat raw retrieved examples (DC, ReasoningBank WebArena 48.8 vs AWM 44.1 vs Synapse 42.1, BoT at 12% of multi-query cost), but ExpeL finds insights win on HotpotQA (36 vs 31) and trajectories on ALFWorld (55 vs 50).
agent_test: Run whole solution vs distilled rule vs template per task type at equal prompt tokens.

claim: Edit gain shrinks with base accuracy on reasoning (Self-Refine math 64.1 to 64.1, 74.8 to 75.0, 92.9 to 93.1) but a retrieval-plus-adaptation pipeline kept its gain from 8B to 671B on a low-base task (CBR-DDI +20.6 / +23.3 / +15.9 over Naive-CBR). Frontier 2026 models untested.
agent_test: Run the edit step on our strongest model, split items by base accuracy.

claim: The diagnosis step is what makes an edit pay: specific actionable feedback beats generic and none (Self-Refine Sentiment 43.2 / 31.2 / 0; Code Opt 27.5 / 26.0 / 24.8); Self-Debugging explanation adds 2 to 3 points without tests, more with tests. Equal-token cost of a separate diagnosis call is untested.
agent_test: Compare diagnose-then-edit vs edit-only at equal tokens.

claim: Failure-derived lessons help when distilled, hurt when stored raw: ReasoningBank 46.5 to 49.7 with failures, AWM 44.4 to 42.2, Synapse 40.6 to 41.7 (WebArena Shopping). This is post-hoc lesson learning, not CHEF-style pre-emptive prediction.
agent_test: Add a lessons-from-failures item type; test with and without.
